summary: T3 rework after review (reviewed commit f3dc2d9). Fixed the secondary-button label that was laid out in white and so ignored its state ink; added a painted-shape regression test that provably fails against the old code; substituted every duplicated colour/shadow token with the theme owner T2 now provides (values verified identical, one owner for KeycapMode); made format_key_for_display char-safe for multi-byte names with new tests; corrected the resolve_dpad comment; and set the secondary button to content + 2 * 13px with its icon following the state ink. The branch still lacks the integration glue (module registration, egui_kittest dev-dependency), so T3 compile/test/clippy evidence comes from an out-of-tree scratch crate that now also uses T2's real theme.rs from agent/integration.

review_actions.id: R1 low + R2 low - format_key_for_display panicked on multi-byte names
review_actions.required: Compute the halfway point over char_indices() and use chars().count() for the >= 7, <= 2, <= 4 and <= 6 length classifications; keep the ASCII assertions green and add multi-byte cases.
review_actions.changed: The split threshold and both size classifications now count characters; the midpoint comes from `char_boundary_at_half`, which maps the halfway character count onto a byte offset with `char_indices().nth`. The digit split is unchanged because `str::find` already returns a char boundary, with a comment saying so.
review_actions.evidence: New test `multi_byte_names_split_without_panicking`: `가나다라마바사` (7 chars / 21 bytes) splits into 가나다라 + 마바사 at 12.0; `가나다라마` (5 chars / 15 bytes) stays on one line at 11.0; `F한` (2 chars / 4 bytes) keeps 18.0; `가나다라마바4` splits on the digit. The old byte-based midpoint panicked on the first case. All five ASCII assertions in `format_key_for_display_splits_compound_keys` and the autoscale assertions are unchanged and green.
